To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
The annealed diluted antiferromagnet (ADA) model is a good description of the cuprate high temperature superconductors.

(a) The critical temperature of the annealed diluted antiferromagnetic system is proportional to the inverse of the correlation length, (b) The critical temperature is proportional to the square of the density of holes in the conduction band, and (c) The critical temperature increases linearly as a function of the inverse of the square of the distance between the holes in the con-duction band.
the critical temperature of high-temperature superconductors can be explained by a mean field theory of the annealed diluted antiferromagnet.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the magnetic and transport properties of high temperature superconductors.
the study of magnetic and superconducting properties of the high T c oxides.
the physics of strongly interacting electron systems.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the superconducting phase of the cuprate perovskites is a result of the interplay of two competing phases, the antiferromagnet and the superconductor, which are coupled by the charge carriers, and that this competition is controlled by the doping.
the superconductivity in the cuprates has a strong magnetic origin.
the superconductivity in La 2− Sr x CuO y is a BCS-like phenomenon.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have shown how to calculate the superconducting transition temperature in an annealed system, and we have applied this formalism to a quasi-two-dimensional antiparallel spin antiferromagnet, which is the appropriate model for high temperature superconductivity in La 2−x Sr x CuO.
the critical temperature is a function of doping and the strength of the nearest neighbor exchange interaction.
the critical temperature of high T c superconductors is not a function of the doping alone but depends also on the magnetic properties of the material.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the high temperature superconductivity is not an anomalous phenomenon but a natural consequence of the physics of a diluted antiferromagnet.
the superconductivity is a consequence of the annealed nature of the magnetism.
the critical temperature is not determined solely by the density of states at the Fermi energy, but also by the strength of the effective pairing interaction.
